messages:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — thinking about how we store/serialize saved filters for the console. We need a single encoding that can express per-route defaults, per-model overrides, sampling hints, and quota scope. Current URL + local state is getting messy.
Jia Park: +1. can you sketch what you mean by "sampling hints"? unsure how that fits into saved query semantics. :thinking:
Maria Chen: sampling hint = telemetry sampling rate suggestion for that view (+ optional eval/test prompt set). Not enforced, just UI hint for the console telemetry pipeline. Example: when you save a model-heavy view we might suggest 1% sample to avoid cost blowouts.
Samir Rao: Curious about encode shape — do we keep single query param blob or multiple params? single blob feels tidy but brittle across versions.
Owen Walker: Backend perspective: single JSON blob works but we need a version field and migration path. We already have consumers that parse ?q=... for deep links. If we change shape we should support v1/v2 for 6 months.
Maria Chen: Proposal: new saved-filter contract: {"v": "2", "scope": "route|model|global", "filters": [...], "telemetry": {"sample": 0.01, "evalSetId": "e-123"}, "quotaHint": {"perTokenBudget": 100000} }
Nora Li: That seems workable. Two concerns: 1) telemetry.sample should be advisory — downstream ingestion must ignore if the route is under strict sampling by infra. 2) evalSetId must be validated (internal-only ids).
Jia Park: UX/console note: defaulting behavior when both route and model filters exist — we should have a deterministic precedence: explicit route-scope saved filter wins, then model-scope, then global. Otherwise users get confused.
Samir Rao: Agree precedence makes sense. Also suggest we store a small human-readable label in the blob so deep links are less opaque for sharing.
Owen Walker: On quotaHint — we can't enforce client-side hints. But we can wire it into route capacity previews and cost estimates in the UI. Backend will ignore quotaHint unless an admin enables an opt-in enforcement flag.
Maria Chen: Sounds good. Next question: API surface. Do we add a new route POST /api/console/saved-filters (v2) that accepts the blob and returns a stable id? or reuse savedquery endpoints?
Jia Park: New endpoint is cleaner. Keep savedquery for legacy. New one should support patch semantics and an exportable JSON blob for infra. Also include ETag for optimistic concurrency.
Nora Li: For telemetry linking, when a saved filter includes evalSetId we should push a small mapping event to our evals service: {type: "saved_filter_bound", id: "sf-...", eval: "e-123"} so quality alerts can be tied back.
Samir Rao: UX rollout idea: soft-launch v2 in the console behind a flag, surface migration button for older savedqueries to convert to v2. Make migration idempotent.
Owen Walker: Deployment ops: deploy-bot will add the v2 handler in canary and we should keep both handlers live. Plan: 1) deploy API v2, 2) enable console flag for 20% of users, 3) allow migration UI, 4) keep v1 for 6 months.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: console-api/v2 -> canary. changelist: saved-filters v2 API, ETag support, telemetry hook.
Maria Chen: Action items: Jia - API spec + example blobs, Owen - canary deploy plan + compatibility test, Nora - evals mapping proto, Samir - migration UX copy + label behavior. I'll follow up with a short RFC. :thumbsup:
Jia Park: I'll post the OpenAPI snippet in #eng-platform later today and include sample deep link encodings (both URL-encoded blob and compact query params).
Nora Li: Quick question — do we allow saved filters to include model-quantization hints? that could change cost estimates.
Maria Chen: Yes as a non-enforced hint (quantProfile: "int8" etc.). We should also surface it in the cost preview.
Samir Rao: ok cool. I sketched the label and precedence microcopy. will drop screenshots in the thread soon.
Owen Walker: I'll add an integration test that asserts v1 requests still return old shape and v2 returns the blob with v: "2".
Maria Chen: Great — thanks all. RFC by EOD tomorrow.
